newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan April consumer prices up 0.51 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan April consumer prices up 0.51 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's April consumer price index rose 0.51 percent compared to April 1996, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics said on Monday.
April's wholesale price index was 2.63 percent compared to April 1996, the directorate said.
April's consumer price index rise was significantly lower than an average forecast of 1.224 percent compiled from Friday's Reuters poll of Taiwan economists.
The CPI rise also was well below the central bank's full-year 1997 inflation forecast of around 3.0 percent and the same target set by the cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development.
The directorate attributed the low inflation to falls in pork prices following the outbreak of a hog epidemic.
It said the epidemic, which has decimated consumer demand in pork since it erupted in March, caused wholesale pork prices in April to plunge by 45 percent and retail prices to drop 20 percent.
The 0.51 percent growth was Taiwan's lowest monthly year-on-year inflation rise since October of 1991, the directorate said in a statement.
Directorate director Chan Teh-song said the low inflation would benefit Taiwan's export-driven economy.
"The low inflation should increase the competitiveness of our export products," Chan told reporters.
